subject.title: Memory compaction blocks main processing lane, causing unresponsive bot for 10+ minutes

question: Should OpenClaw isolate or preempt compaction/memoryFlush from the foreground session lane, or keep the current foreground lane model with shorter timeouts and diagnostic recovery?
rationale: The bug is source-backed, but the durable fix changes scheduler/session-state ordering guarantees for interactive turns versus context maintenance.

options.title: Isolate compaction lane
options.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.

options.title: Preempt foreground maintenance
options.body: Keep the lane model but make compaction/memoryFlush abortable and reschedulable when user messages arrive, preserving stricter ordering at the cost of scheduler complexity.

options.title: Accept timeout mitigation
options.body: Treat the current 180-second timeout and stuck-session recovery as sufficient mitigation, leaving foreground turns blocked during active compaction windows.

recommendation.title: Isolate compaction lane
recommendation.body: Run compaction and memoryFlush in a dedicated low-concurrency lane or worker so foreground user messages can be admitted or acknowledged without waiting for the full maintenance timeout.
